name: ANSI/IEEE cable pothead symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented pothead symbol marking a sealed cable termination where an insulated cable meets an overhead line or bus.
description: Pothead is the traditional North American term for a sealed cable termination, especially at riser poles and outdoor substations. IEEE-style single-line diagrams show it where a cable rises to connect to an overhead line or open bus, often with a lightning arrester beside it.

This illustration is an independent explanation of the convention and is not the IEEE graphic. Modern terminations may be porcelain, polymer or slip-on types, all of which may be called potheads on older drawings. Rating and creepage distance belong in the equipment data.
readingNotes: Look for an arrester at riser pole potheads.
Treat older pothead labels as any sealed termination type.
drawingChecklist: Mark phase identification at the pothead.
distinction: A pothead is a fixed sealed termination; a separable connector can be unplugged.
